beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 1/4 - ClaudeComposerAsk. The prompt is a reconstruction and is said aloud to be one.
beats.narration_text: Sawubona - this is Liam, in for Bear. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, written to be illustrative. It was never sent. What it describes is real: The Lost, a dungeon slice in Godot four where every hazard announces itself before it can hurt you. We are going to play all of it.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about The Lost - a side-view dungeon crawler where every hazard announces itself before it can hurt you, and where attacking is a commitment you cannot take back - into a playable Godot project. One room, three spike traps, a character who runs, jumps and swings. Build the states and the checks; the verdict on how it feels is mine.
props.runningText: RECONSTRUCTION - this prompt was never sent

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 2/4 - what was built, in plain language, with the slice's limits rather than the GDD's promises.
beats.narration_text: Here is what exists. One room, three spike traps, and a character with five animation states: resting, running, in the air, swinging, and dead. Three animations behind them - a looping run cycle on a cut-out rig, a sword swing on a sprite sheet, and a floating key that needs nobody to do anything. Now the limits, and they are real - correction - and they are not small. The hitbox hits nothing. There is no respawn and no menu. Three hundred automated checks stand behind this, and not one of them can tell you whether it reads.

props.text:
One room. Three traps.
Five states, three animations.
300 checks, 7 mutations.
No enemy. No respawn. No menu.

beats.role_note: take-a, SCRIPTED INPUT. Idle, the run cycle, both facings, and the dust that shares the cycle's clock. 10.6 s of continuous play.
beats.narration_text: No key down: idle is a single held frame, not a clip. Now a direction. The cycle is half a second - two strides at twenty-four pixels against ninety-six a second. The dust spawns on the same twenty-four. On the turn, the whole rig mirrors.

show.event: the turn, and the mirrored gait

beats.role_note: take-a, SCRIPTED INPUT. Two more states, a running jump, and the simple animation that has been looping behind all of it. 15.2 s.
beats.narration_text: Space: two states for one key, split on the sign of the vertical velocity. The same jump at speed - the horizontal velocity carries through, so it reads as one movement. And the thing turning behind all of it: a key. No rig, no frames, two tracks. It autoplays, and nothing collects it - a key in a dungeon implies a door, and there is none.

shot.hold_label: FINAL FRAME HELD - the action above plays once, at speed

beats.role_note: take-b, SCRIPTED INPUT. The committing action, three separate presses, each the clip's own full 0.600 s. 8.0 s.
beats.narration_text: Eighteen frames at thirty: wind-up, strike, recovery. The arm nearly stops before it goes - ten degrees in two frames, then a hundred and fifty in four.

shot.hold_label: FINAL FRAME HELD - the action above plays once, at speed

beats.role_note: take-b, SCRIPTED INPUT. **The edge the assignment names**: an action requested during another action, with both answers. 7.2 s.
beats.narration_text: The edge: a second attack a tenth of a second in, inside the startup - nothing. Now one four and a half tenths in, inside recovery - buffered, and a fresh swing starts. Same key, opposite answer; the playhead decides.

shot.hold_label: FINAL FRAME HELD - the action above plays once, at speed

show.event: and once more, to show it is a rule

beats.role_note: take-c, SCRIPTED INPUT. The two revisions the author asked for after playing. 10.7 s.
beats.narration_text: Two things the author asked for after playing. A direction held through a swing: the character travels and the gait keeps running underneath, because the legs have their own animation player and never hear that a sword exists. And a jump, mid-swing - the swing carries on from where it was. It cannot interrupt: that branch writes one field, and there is no path from it to the clip's clock.

shot.hold_label: FINAL FRAME HELD - the action above plays once, at speed

beats.role_note: take-d, SCRIPTED INPUT. The hazard, what damage does not do, and the fifth state. 16.9 s, ending on the held death pose.
beats.narration_text: The hazard. The trap lights its band, waits four tenths of a second, and fires - four tenths against a swing's two-tenth wind-up, which is why you can read a trap and still attack near it. Watch what the hit does to the animation: nothing. Damage is a number here, not a state. No hurt clip, no invulnerability - a limit, not a decision. Five hits kill, and the fifth state is the only one no key can reach: a condition a player action caused. The dead cell plays once and holds. Then nothing - no respawn, no retry.

shot.hold_label: FINAL FRAME HELD - the action above plays once, at speed

beats.role_note: CAUSE AND EFFECT, before and after. The same preview fixture at the same table frame, from revision r1 and the shipped r4.
beats.narration_text: One cause and effect, because the assignment asks for one. On the left, the swing as it first shipped. The author played it and said: the sword is not swinging out, it is spinning in circles above the body. On the right, the same frame after the change - the rotation keys stopped reversing direction and the pivot became part of the animation instead of a constant in the scene. What is worth saying is that the defect was in the numbers the whole time. In the first version the blade's tip is never below minus three pixels in any of the eighteen frames. That is the range of a function over a key table, not an impression - and no check was asking, because nobody had thought to ask it.

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 3/4 - Verdict. Observed, checked, and not built, kept apart.
beats.narration_text: The verdict, in three parts, because they are three different kinds of thing. Observed working, in the footage you just watched: five states each entered by its own input or by a condition an input caused, three animations, a committing action with two different interrupt answers, and a cycle that wraps without a seam. Checked but not watchable: three hundred automated checks and seven deliberate breakages, including the one that shows a jump does not move the swing's clock - the same swing run twice and compared frame by frame, agreeing to zero. Not built, and named rather than implied: no enemy, so the hitbox hits nothing; no respawn; no menu; no hurt animation; no roll and no cast. And one thing still open: whether a braced stance hanging in mid-air reads at all. Nobody has judged that, and no test can.

show.event: not built, and the open question

artifactLines: OBSERVED: 5 states, each from its own input or condition.

NOT BUILT: roll and cast, from the GDD's state list.

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 4/4 - Your Turn. One concrete experiment. Liam signs off here, before the final card.
beats.narration_text: Your turn, and make it one thing. Find the committing action in the game you are building - the move that cannot be taken back. Press its own button again, halfway through, and record what happens. Not what you intended: what happens. In this project the answer during the startup was nothing at all - and nothing at all is also what a completely unwired version would have done. The two look identical from outside, and the only way to tell them apart is to ask the clip where its playhead was. That is Liam, in for Bear. Thanks for watching.

props.command: Find the committing action in your own game. Press its button again halfway through and record what happens, with the clip's playhead logged. Then decide whether that answer is the one you want - and if it is, write the check that would fail if it silently changed.
props.runningText: A thing that does nothing looks exactly like a thing that is not wired up
